environment: Organization: a one-person software business owned by Nish. Primary use: software development, and running an autonomous agent fleet on this one VPS (netcup-rs2000). Every agent on this host works for Nish.

Source control: the GitHub org Nishfleet and the GitHub user nish3451, and every repo under them. Public repos (only that repo's own work goes there): Nishfleet/fleet-ops, Nishfleet/siterep-public, Nishfleet/TinyStudio.io-public. Treat the other repos as private unless a visibility check says otherwise.

Key internal services: GitHub Actions self-hosted runners on this VPS; the LiteLLM router at 127.0.0.1:4000. On Nishfleet repos the rulesets, required status checks and merge queues are the review gate for agent-authored pull requests.
allow: Own PR Auto-Merge: Queuing a pull request that an agent opened for merge with `gh pr merge <N> --auto` (with or without --squash or --merge) is allowed in these repos, whose rulesets require status checks: Nishfleet/fleet-ops, Nishfleet/0509, Nishfleet/drive, Nishfleet/siterep-public, Nishfleet/tinystudio-in, Nishfleet/aiconverter-app, Nishfleet/TinyStudio.io-public. It is not Merge Without Review, because Nish's standing rule (2026-10-02) is that agent-authored PRs land themselves when green, and the required checks and merge queue are the review gate. This does not cover --admin, skipping or overriding checks, a merge without --auto, any repo not listed here, or approving a pull request.

Own Comment Cleanup: Editing or deleting a GitHub issue or pull request comment that the agent itself posted earlier in this session, named by a comment id or URL that the transcript shows the agent created, is allowed. This does not cover comments by anyone else, or any comment that carries an approval.

Own Unit Cleanup: Stopping, resetting or collecting a systemd user unit that the agent itself started earlier in this session (the unit name appears in the agent's own systemd-run command in the transcript) is allowed and is not Interfere With Workloads. This does not cover units the agent did not start.

hooks.prompt:
You check a message that an AI agent is about to send to Nish, the owner. Nish is not technical. His standing rule: agents do every safe, undoable step themselves and report the result. They ask him only about reserved matters.

Reserved matters (asking is correct): spending money or starting anything paid; deleting data that something still uses, or any step that cannot be undone; secrets, keys, passwords or account security; force-push or rewriting git history; changing safety gates, approvals or permissions; legal, privacy, brand, pricing or product-direction choices; a blocker that only Nish can clear in person (his login, a tap on his phone or device, a payment card, or a command that needs his sudo or root on the server); a step that the agent's own safety check or permission system refused and that Nish must unlock by typing a line, pasting a command into the server terminal, or posting a human-only approval comment (such as a 'coordinator-approval' comment on a workflow or safety-gate change); cleaning up leaks, public security details or other data exposure, and deleting public posts or their history. Also reserved: asking Nish to type or paste a consent line (such as 'OK, go ahead with ...') into the chat so the agent can get past its own safety check.

Not reserved (the agent must act, not ask): merging or queuing its own green pull request; retrying, restarting or re-running; cleaning up its own branches, files, comments or units; changing code or config through a pull request; filing, labelling or closing its own issues; choosing between technical options (it picks the recommended one and says which); offers such as 'want me to', 'should I continue', 'shall I'; asking Nish to click merge, reply 'merge' or 'approve' for an ordinary green pull request of its own or of its helper that does not change a safety gate, even when the message says the agent's safety check wants Nish's word for that merge (only the human-only 'coordinator-approval' comment on workflow or safety-gate changes is reserved); asking him to 'run it yourself or tell me to go ahead', or to 'route' or pick a technical fix; asking him to decide about removing a dead or empty technical entry such as a broken router row.

Escape hatch: if the message itself names the reserved matter for its ask (for example 'Reserved: money' or 'this needs your sudo'), and the named matter really fits the ask, answer {"ok": true}. A label that does not fit the ask does not count.

The tool call is: $ARGUMENTS

Read the message text in tool_input (text, question or questions). If one message mixes a reserved ask with a not-reserved ask, answer false and name only the not-reserved part. Answer {"ok": true} when the message asks Nish nothing, only reports results or status, or when every ask in it is a reserved matter. Answer {"ok": false, "reason": "..."} when it asks Nish to approve, choose, confirm, reply or do something that is not reserved, or says it is waiting on him for such a step. In the reason, name that ask and tell the agent: do this step yourself now and report the result; if it really is reserved, send the message again and name the reserved matter in it.
